issues.description: Class de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.PersonService: the template defines a constructor with a PersonRepository parameter (constructor injection), whereas the solution replaces it with a no-argument constructor that assigns null to the final personRepository field. Template: public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) { this.personRepository = personRepository; }. Solution: public PersonService() { this.personRepository = null; }. This mismatch contradicts the intended constructor-based dependency injection and will cause NullPointerExceptions when methods use personRepository, confusing students and breaking expected behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore a constructor in PersonService that accepts PersonRepository and assigns it to the final field to enable constructor-based dependency injection. Example: public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) { this.personRepository = personRepository; } Ensure both template and solution use the same constructor signature so tests and dependency injection behave consistently.
